source_title: U.S. Census 2023 Nonemployer Statistics for NAICS 115210
observation: The broad NAICS 115210 category contains about 62,000 nonemployer businesses and $3.23 billion in receipts.
denominator: US nonemployer businesses classified to NAICS 115210
limitations: The category includes boarding, breeding and other animal-production support alongside farriers.
It does not isolate iPhone users or therapeutic-case farriers.

source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Caring for your horse's hooves
observation: University of Minnesota Extension recommends hoof care every 6 to 8 weeks in summer and every 6 to 12 weeks in winter.
unit: weeks, upper end of summer interval
limitations: Care guidance establishes a recurring cycle, not app demand or professional service retention.

source_title: American Farriers Journal: Footcare and Farrier Business Insights
observation: The trade publication reports about eight annual trim or shoe cycles per typical horse and approximately 370 weekly driving miles and 301 horses for a full-time farrier profile.
unit: annual hoof-care cycles per typical horse, reported estimate
denominator: sample size and response rate not published on the accessible page
limitations: Trade-publication estimates; sample n and response rate were not disclosed.
The profile is not the exact therapeutic iPhone segment.

source_title: American Farriers Journal: Farrier Business Trends Reveal Shifting Priorities
observation: The trade survey says farriers still prefer pen and paper for schedules, invoices and horse records and that phone or computer use for those tasks declined from 2024.
denominator: sample size and response rate not published on the accessible page
limitations: The result cannot be safely generalized without sampling details.
It does not isolate therapeutic workflows.

observation: The Farriers App lists a $59 monthly plan and $25 per additional user with horse records, photos, veterinary documents, scheduling and reporting.
limitations: List price is not transaction, retention, or incremental companion budget.

observation: Best Farrier lists a $30.99 monthly plan with horse history, photos, scheduling, routes and invoicing.
limitations: List price is not realized payment or product-fit evidence.

observation: Hoofproof already offers hoof photo and video records, annotation, side-by-side comparison and voice transcription at no download cost.
limitations: Feature presence does not prove traction or retention.
A narrower consented veterinarian-handoff behavior remains untested.

source_title: AAEP Position on Roles of Healthcare Providers in Veterinary Medicine
observation: AAEP's attending-veterinarian oversight boundary supports testing a standardized, consented farrier-to-veterinarian observation handoff instead of diagnostic automation.
limitations: This is an inference from professional-scope guidance, not observed demand or payment for the proposed packet.

observation: AFA lists 50 chapters, an annual convention, a member directory and publication channels.
limitations: Channel existence is not product traction, CAC, or conversion.

source_title: AAEP Position on Roles of Healthcare Providers in Veterinary Medicine
observation: AAEP describes farriers as unlicensed allied healthcare providers and emphasizes attending-veterinarian oversight when work enters veterinary healthcare scope.
limitations: State law may vary and requires legal review; this is not legal advice.

observation: Apple provides a publication path for camera, microphone, local storage, sharing and subscription workflows subject to privacy, consent, security, retention and deletion requirements.
limitations: Compliance does not assure approval and rules can change.

observation: Public sources do not isolate active US farriers using iPhone, handling therapeutic cases, or paying for hoof-history software.
limitations: Only broad NAICS and trade-survey proxies are available.
